messages.body_plain:
Over the past few years, we've been trying to reduce the impact of non-free software licenses, but the CRAN akima package for interpolation is under:

http://www.acm.org/publications/policies/softwarecrnotice

which is "solely for academic, research and other similar noncommercial uses, subject to the following conditions ..."

This means that all CRAN packages that Depends: on it are limited in propagation. Soon, at the request of institutions using CRAN, including universities, we'll be providing a stronger filter allowing them to avoid potential creeping license risk by limiting downloads to free licenses with only free Depends:.

So we need a clean-room re-coding of Akima's algorithm for interpolation.

Could the administrators consider adding this to the table in the Wiki? Would a short description to link to the table help? Daniel McMillen (CRAN/McSpatial) has kindly agreed to co-mentor.

Roger Bivand

messages.subject_clean: Proposal for Google Summer code 2013 with R
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

During my internship in a National Institute of Statistics in a developing country, I have seen people finding difficult and spending a lot of time trying to balance their National Account (Production+ Importation+…=Intermediate Consumption + Investment + Stock variation+…). This is because there is lack of financial resources to conduct survey (as a consequence, there is a lack of data) but also a lack of competences and human resource involved in National Account Service. The main challenge of balancing National Account is that: when one changes the column matrix of Intermediate Consumption, He needs to change all the repartition of Intermediate Consumption within each branches (sub-sectors) of the economy but also, the repartition of production within branches (because, National Account says that the ratio of Intermediate Consumption on Production should be slightly constant in short-period. This is often called “Technical coefficient”). That’s why I’ve lead some reflections for automatically balancing National Account according to these constraints (economic constraint + mathematical constraint) with R. I’ve been able to succeed doing the equilibrium with simple linear algebra but need to pursue my efforts (my short-run goal is to build a package) and why not discuss with experts in the area. That’s why I’m sending this proposal hoping to be supported by a monitor interested in this project. My long-run Goal is to be able to use this framework to study impacts of politics in a developing economy. According to me, this framework is particularly relevant in developing countries facing lack of resources to conduct survey and may be a starting point to improve National Account Statistics in these countries.

H.R

PS: I apologize for my english!

(instead of extending something which already exists) is to ask what
hole does it fill. What I'm hearing is that R fills holes in SAS,
Access, etc., but what I'd like to hear is what hole in R you'd like
to fill.

Cheers,

Hello,

I am Junaid from National University of Sciences and Technology. Currently I am a student of MS Electrical Engineering.

I have an idea for developing Bayesian Chain Classifier for multi dimensional classification. Recently, I was looking for developing an anomaly detector that can be used for the detection of zero day attacks (where rule based IDS fails). This was based over the application of machine learning and stochastic concepts. Due to multi dimensional nature of the problem, the classification of traffic (whether it falls into friendly or hostile class) depends upon multiple features. Hence, Bayesian Chain Classifier appears to be a suitable candidate for that [1].

I haven't done much prior work over r-project. But I haven't found any implementation of Bayesian Chain Classifier in r-project. So the idea is to add support for it.

References:
[1] J. H. Zaragoza, L. E. Sucar, E. F. Morales, C. Bielza and P. Larranaga, "Bayesian Chain Classifiers for Multidimensional Classification," Proceedings of 22nd International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence.

I would like to have feedback over this idea.

Regards,
Junaid

Thanks for your expression of interest. The test for prospective students will involve reviewing and analysing the use of the functions in the akima package in a sample of packages in CRAN, the comprehensive R archive network. Use of awk/sed on files in the man/ directories of the packages using akima may be a good way in - spotting and extracting uses of functions in akima; the source packages are all on CRAN in predictable locations for a given mirror.

I attach an RData file to load into R giving the names of packages that depend on, import or suggest akima. Reading the R admin. manual may show how the package system works; the pkgDepTools package from Bioconductor was used here to analyse the dependency tree of packages and generate the two character (string) vectors of names, which may not be unique.

Some uses are trivial, not altering the defaults used in the akima package, but others permit the user to modify arguments, and these will be the best test of a drop-in replacement. The test will be to set up an effective benchmark, so that we can know to what extent the drop-in replacement gives users the same or similar results, and the same or similar control over the results.

Of course, the examples in the help files in the akima package itself are a good place to start, but the other packages using akima may exercise it ways not anticipated by the package authors.

Hello,
I am a PhD student of the Mathematical Methods and Representation
Department at University of A Coru�a.
I started my PhD in Civil Engineer majoring in Transportation in 2010
and my thesis is focused on discrete choice modeling. Since that, I've
been working with R.

Usually, I use the mlogit package [1] for estimate my models on R. This
package use, to do the description of the variables involved in the
model, extended model formulas which are build upon formula objects
provided by the Formula package [2]. However, this are not very
practical for models with advanced utility specification because the
formula object force to have the same variables for all the utility
specification of the alternatives. And the best, for a realistic
representation of choice behaviour, would be that you could be able to
use a different specification for each alternative.

In the scope of the Google Summer of Code I'm very interested in
developing the required methods and functions needed to improve the
mlogit package and fix this limitation.
I think this will allow easily estimate advanced model structures on R,
like other software packages for discrete choice estimation do (e.g.
Biogeme [3]).

If you have other suggestions related with discrete choice modeling I'll
be very happy to discuss about it and see if I could work on it!
I am a linux user and have programming experience with C++, Fortran and
Python. Also, I have a big background on maths (I have a master's degree
in civil engineering).

Thanks,

Dear All,

I am Khurram and I am a PhD student in Computer Vision at UCF. I am interested in working for R-project and would like to contribute to the open source community. In todays world where everyone owns a camera, there is a huge amount of data in the form of images and videos that people try to analyze and perform useful things like: actions recognition, object detection, tracking, etc. After having a detailed look at the current packages related to Computer Vision in the R repository, I felt the need for a good package, that would cover major algorithms in this area and would be something to build upon for later programmers to come. I compiled the following list of algorithms/functions that are being used frequently in MATLAB/OpenCV/etc and would be something really useful for users of R-project:-

1.Edge Detection: Canny, Sobel, Prewitt, Marr Hildreth

2.Feature Extraction: Harris Corner Detector, HOG (Histogram of Oriented Gradients)

3.Optical Flow: Horn & Shunk, Lucas-Kanade with Pyramids

Hi Paul,

The 'EBImage' covers only a small percentage of the things I have proposed.

These include: 1) Spatial Transformation (resize, rotate & translate) 2) Color Transformation (Only Color to Grayscale and vice versa) 3) Basic  Image filtering (Convolving filters to get image derivative and blur images). It doesn't include anyone of the sophisticated techniques for edge detection such as Canny, Marr Hildreth, etc. 4) Morphological Operation (dilate, erode, etc) 5) Segmentation: Though it says segmentation, but what it actually does is that it finds connected components in binary images. Segmentation in RGB/Color images is a totally different domain where the objective is to represent images into something more meaningful (such as objects,etc) and able to analyze them.

In summary the 'EBImage' package partially covers section 8 & 9 of my proposal.

Thanks,
Khurram

http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2013

methods such that the methods can be applied to data sets that are
large in the number of variables or observations. I would serve as the
mentor and I already found an interested and highly qualified student.
